properties.name: Milton Keynes curated visitor boundary
properties.methodology: Morphological closing of the existing curated visitor boundary using a 100 metre outward and inward buffer. This preserves its deliberate visitor extensions while filling internal omissions for connected parks, river corridors and visitor green spaces.

project.boundarySource: Curated Milton Keynes visitor boundary with reviewed OSM public green-space extensions
project.researchNotes:
Townscape Guides audit completed 2026-08-09. The unchanged ONS 2024 built-up area is the active inclusion boundary. Historic England designations and public current OpenStreetMap visitor facilities were filtered point-in-polygon. Historic England official list-entry date enrichment completed 2026-08-09: 21 of 365 statutory records now carry defensible date evidence; unresolved entries were individually checked and retained as unknown. Bedfordshire and Northamptonshire standalone attraction audit added 2026-08-09. These are explicit Home-only regional destinations and do not alter the host town planner or tourist rating.

Broad visitor-attraction editorial discovery pass 2026-08-13: expanded See discovery beyond historic records using a local OSM extract. Automatically discovered additions remain below Recommended until source-backed editorial review.

touristAppeal.label: Worth a planned stop
touristAppeal.summary: Milton Keynes supports a coherent half-day visit through MK Gallery, Milton Keynes Museum and Xscape Milton Keynes.

townGuide.headline: Modernist landmarks, bold public art and a city built around green space
townGuide.intro: Milton Keynes is best explored as a designed landscape: combine MK Gallery and central public art with Campbell Park, Willen Lake and the Peace Pagoda, then choose a museum or family attraction.
perfectFor: A genuinely distinctive destination for modern urbanism, culture and easy outdoor recreation.

suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Start with MK Gallery and the central public-art route, cross Campbell Park, then continue to Willen Lake and the Peace Pagoda.
